analysis.title: US Public Policy: Midterm Election Results: Decisive for Democrats
key_insights: Democrats have won control of the House and Senate, although some races are still being counted. The results point toward MS's 'cohesive' Democratic majority scenario.

In this scenario, uncertainty from the change in control can be a headwind to equities at the index level, similar to the 2022 midterm volatility. A potential delay of SNAP/Medicaid cuts is a tailwind to consumer sectors and adds some upside risk to growth forecasts.

A party-line reconciliation route is closed. That removes the main source of upside to Treasury's borrowing needs. Delaying SNAP/Medicaid cuts works the other way, but the effect is likely small against a $2 trillion deficit.

Four policy areas to focus on: fiscal (OBBBA SNAP and Medicaid cuts may be rolled back, extended or softened around fiscal deadlines, with deficits staying near 6% of GDP), executive-led policy (tariffs, geopolitics, USMCA review, deregulation and export controls persist), data center restrictions, and signaling around 2028.

Data center restrictions are the main AI risk. The binding levers (interconnection, large-load rate design, siting, tax abatements) sit with state commissions, legislatures and county boards, so the exposure is likely limited to specific jurisdictions. The most important result for data center development was the Texas governor's race.

The election of Democrat Gina Hinojosa in Texas raises policy risk for the pace of data center approvals and construction. Her platform included a moratorium on new data center approvals, and MS sees a risk that many projects are delayed significantly.

In Ohio, Democrat Amy Acton's election creates significant risk of data center delays. The largest project at risk is a 10 GW project involving NVIDIA and a major US AI lab. Amazon's 1.5 GW Fayette County facility is under construction. Ohio enacted a moratorium on new data center tax exemption requests in May.

Legislation targeting AI buildout (reversing OBBBA immediate expensing, a tax on compute) is possible as groundwork for 2029, but MS thinks it is unlikely to materialize given the president's opposition.

US equities: since 1982, large caps have gained about 15% cap-weighted and 16% equal-weighted in the six months after midterms, and about 22% over the following year. Investors broadly anticipated a Democratic sweep with a narrow Senate majority, so the Texas governor win could add near-term volatility. MS thinks it could mark the final phase of the rolling correction. Renewed military escalation with Iran or new tariffs are near-term risks.

Cross-asset: MS keeps its overweight on global equities versus underweight on core fixed income. The view rests on the AI capex cycle staying intact. Corporate credit issuance is expected to stay elevated on digital infrastructure funding needs, which could pressure spreads, particularly in lower-quality credit.

AI sentiment: given losses by incumbents in key state and local races, this outcome could weigh most on AI sentiment. MS expects an idiosyncratic headwind that leaves the broad AI capex narrative intact but splits regions that permit new data centers from those that do not.

US rates: Democratic control of both chambers rules out a Republican reconciliation bill when the new Congress convenes in January. Pre-election pricing reflected limited expectations of that supply (prediction markets gave single-digit odds to unified Republican control). Delayed SNAP/Medicaid cuts could modestly increase 2-7y issuance, so MS sees only modest underperformance in the belly.

Debt limit: unless the lame-duck session raises it, Treasury stays on schedule to raise coupon auction sizes in February 2027. Democrats could attach priorities to a later increase. Bills maturing around the x-date could cheapen, and late-3Q27 SOFR/FF basis longs could become more attractive.

If state and local restrictions slow data center construction, a smaller AI-related bond issuance pipeline could reduce long-dated duration supply and richen 10s and 30s. MS treats this as a risk scenario, not its forecast.

USD/FX: near-term trading is expected to follow MS's defense regime, favoring JPY, CHF and EUR against USD. AUD may lag on crosses because of its sensitivity to AI equity sentiment. CAD may underperform versus low yielders on tariff risk. NOK/SEK may face temporary downward pressure.
US economics: the outlook for resilient growth and gradual disinflation is intact, with more upside to growth. A delay to SNAP and Medicaid cuts could add up to 0.4pp to 2027 personal consumption.

AI-related financing could shift toward chip financing relative to power-shell financing. By the chip-installation stage, construction and energization (the activities most exposed to policy) are typically complete. This could contribute to a more sustained flattening of credit curves.

Healthcare: a Democratic sweep is likely a positive for Medicaid-focused managed care (CNC, MOH), with a more muted response for diversified managed care (UNH, CVS). Medicare Advantage names such as HUM could ebb on a knee-jerk reaction. MS thinks the stock reaction is disproportionately favorable for Medicaid.

Lame duck: a continuing resolution funds the government through December 11. The FY27 NDAA is expected to pass by year-end, possibly with export control provisions (MATCH Act, AI OVERWATCH, Chip Security, RASA). The direction of travel is more restrictions, driven by Congress.

A GOP-only 'Reconciliation 3.0' in the lame duck is viewed as an uphill battle and would be the main upside risk to Treasury borrowing needs. MS rates strategists estimate the debt limit becomes binding by March 2027 and the x-date falls in late 3Q27.

US-China: further Trump-Xi meetings are possible at APEC in Shenzhen on Nov 18-19 and the G20 in Miami on Dec 14-15. The base case is managed competition with limited agreements and limited escalation.

Texas data center background: interconnection requests reached about 474 GW, more than 5x ERCOT's record peak demand, with data centers about 90% of new requests. In August, Texas paused parts of its interconnection process after Gov. Abbott ordered an audit.

Texas governor powers: an executive order for a temporary pause, appointments to the PUCT (6-year terms, two coming up in 2027), and direction to agencies on permitting. Tax changes, local veto power, ratepayer protections and union hiring requirements need legislation.

Texas-exposed names (CIFR, MARA, GLXY, SEI, VST, CEG, AEP, SRE, CNP, NRG, power equipment) could be under pressure. MS expects to cut its assumed probabilities for many Texas data center projects, especially those in the Batch process (GLXY Helios II, CIFR Colchis, MARA's project). Projects under construction (GLXY Helios I Phases II and III, HUT Beacon Point, CIFR's projects) are seen as less exposed.

IPPs: knee-jerk underperformance is expected, led by VST, then NRG and CEG. TLN and PEG have no Texas exposure and should outperform relatively. MS values VST's current assets at about $180/share versus a $140 price, CEG at $249 versus $263, NRG at $129 versus $96, and TLN at $430 versus $357. A modest decline in ERCOT forwards is expected.

Power equipment: MS expects underperformance across the group on slower data center growth risk, with multiple compression. GEV is the most diversified and has limited earnings impact. Engine suppliers such as INIO could see slower bookings in 2029+. Solaris is called out as having valuation support: contracts support $81 versus a $69 stock.

Utilities: CNP is most sensitive (highest Texas exposure, ~11% premium, well-owned). SRE, AEP, XEL and ETR also have Texas exposure and could underperform on modest earnings revisions and multiple compression. Gas utilities (OGS, ATO) see no direct impact. Investors may shift into defensive utilities (AEE, ED, DUK) and stay in ETR.

Data center REITs: EQIX has nine Texas facilities (~3% of 280 global data centers). DLR has measurable exposure (Dallas metro 4.2% of annualized rent in 3Q26), but scarcity value for power-secured assets could rise. Both have shown high beta to AI headline volatility. MS stays positive on colocation.

WULF is insulated from Texas regulation (next likely project in Kentucky), APLD is a relative beneficiary, and Bloom Energy (BE) is well positioned if Democrats push back on gas turbine pollution and noise.

MS has high conviction that WMB is materially mispriced relative to behind-the-meter data center power growth that should become clearer over the next 12-24 months. It sees attractive asymmetry and expects terminal value concerns on WMB's power projects to fade.

CIFR valuation: existing leases and Bitcoin mining assets are worth $18/share, with a 56% probability weighting on additional sites signing leases, giving a $51.50 price target. The bear case is $5/share. GLXY SOTP is $43/share.

tension_points.bull_case: MS expects the AI capex narrative to remain intact, with restrictions limited to specific states and only a bifurcation between permitting and non-permitting regions. Power-secured existing facilities gain scarcity value.
